look_here_first: Look at the base/collar and then the seedhead: a tall warm-season rhizomatous clump with a broad airy pyramidal panicle and a conspicuously hairy ligule/collar zone.

project_inclusion.range_basis: 24-county boundary audit 2026-10-14: Hays, Blanco qualify; Val Verde out-of-zone and excluded from PASS. Previous evidence preserved in range_audit; third approved county pending.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Occurrence is not treated as nativity; introduced records do not count toward the three-county native threshold.

range_audit.reason: Old PASS required 3 approved counties, but only 2 in stored evidence are inside zone. Not an assertion that other local wild populations are absent.
range_audit.original_range_basis: Kew/POWO accepts Panicum virgatum and lists Texas in its native range. Hagenbuch & Lemke's Texas Hill Country grass appendix explicitly records Hays County (Bierner 90-208, TEX-LL). The same appendix explicitly records Blanco County (Breckenridge 559, SWT). The same appendix explicitly records Val Verde County (Smith & Butterwick 202, TEX-LL).

best_field_traits: ligule a ciliolate membrane with conspicuous collar hairs
morphology_keys.joey_family_training: Use the completed Poaceae morphology framework: inflorescence architecture first, then spikelets, glumes, lemma/palea, awns, ligule, collar, sheath and nodes.

comparisons.key_distinctions: Panicum coloratum: Kleingrass can resemble switchgrass in the panicle, but is an introduced African bunchgrass with a firm knotty base; switchgrass is native and rhizomatous. Panicum hallii: Hall's panicum is much shorter, glaucous, mostly basal-leaved, and has a smaller stiffer panicle.
